topline.text: The DfE has told the NEU that this year's 3.5% teacher pay rise will be fully funded after all, via roughly £500m freed up by lower local government pension contributions — potentially averting the strike ballot due to open on 3 October.
topline.action: NEU's national executive meets on 24 September to decide whether to stand the ballot down.

topline.text: Newfield Secondary's first Ofsted report since Mercia Learning Trust's 2025 takeover rated attendance/behaviour and inclusion at 'strong standard', a marked turnaround from last year's parent and pupil protests over curriculum cuts.
topline.action: A useful local case study on inclusion recovering after a difficult MAT transition.

diary.text: DfE's twin SEND/EOTAS reform consultations close tomorrow — last call to respond before proposals are firmed up.

items.lede: Teachers' pay rise now fully funded, DfE confirms.
items.body: Education secretary Lucy Powell told the NEU that recent local government pension scheme revaluations free up roughly £500m for schools this year, meaning the pay award won't need to come out of existing budgets after all. The NEU's national executive meets on 24 September to decide whether to stand down its planned ballot.
items.action: Worth holding off on any budget-planning adjustments until the 24 September decision is confirmed.

items.lede: Suspension rates keep falling — but the disadvantage gap doesn't.
items.body: New FFT Education Datalab analysis of autumn term 2025/26 finds secondary suspension and exclusion rates still falling, extending last year's post-pandemic reversal, while primary years 1-4 saw a small rise. Disadvantaged pupils remain far more likely than their peers to be excluded or suspended. Figures are FFT's own analysis, flagged here as provisional pending the DfE's official autumn release.
items.action: Worth checking against your own autumn-term figures if disadvantage-gap language is going into this year's SEF.

items.lede: Newfield's first Ofsted since the Mercia takeover: a turnaround story.
items.body: Inspectors called Newfield Secondary (Norton Lees) 'warm, caring, calm, orderly and respectful' in its first report since Mercia Learning Trust took over in 2025, rating attendance/behaviour and inclusion at 'strong standard' — a marked shift after last year's contentious takeover, which included a pupil walkout over proposed arts cuts.
items.action: A live example of inclusion recovering post-MAT-transition — useful if you're advising other schools going through the same.

box.text: FFT Education Datalab's estimate of the combined suspension and exclusion rate in secondary schools, autumn term 2025/26 — down from 4.1% the year before.
